Watch the idea ↓

Put it down. Plug it in. Switch it on.

The starting point

You already know
how to use it.

A lamp should begin with a switch. Everything clever should earn its place after that.

We're developing a lamp that learns from the way you use it: the evenings you reach for the light, the times you turn it down, the moments you switch it off.

The aim is simple. Keep the familiar control. Give you fewer reasons to need it.

A little more in step

Your evening.
Your say.

An ordinary evening

You reach for the switch.

The light should respond straight away. Learning must never get between you and a working lamp.

A pattern takes shape

It starts to notice.

Repeated choices can offer useful clues. We're exploring how those clues and the light in the room can guide a helpful response.

Tonight is different

You change your mind.

Turn it on or off yourself. Your choice should take priority, without the lamp immediately undoing it.

These are design requirements, not demonstrated product capabilities. The way learning works is still being developed.

What should stay ordinary

A place on
your table.

No new habit to learn just to get some light.

Our requirements are a physical on/off control and a core job that works locally, without an account, companion app, internet connection or subscription.

It also needs to be reliable, attainable and straightforward to look after. Those are part of making a better lamp.
